name: Pituitary Resistance to Thyroid Hormone
aliases: Selective Pituitary Resistance to Thyroid Hormone

criteria.description: Elevated serum free T4 and/or free T3 levels with non-suppressed or elevated TSH
Clinical and biochemical evidence of resistance localized to the pituitary gland (e.g., inappropriate TSH secretion despite elevated thyroid hormones)
Identification of mutations in the thyroid hormone receptor beta (THRB) gene affecting pituitary sensitivity
Exclusion of other causes of elevated thyroid hormones such as thyroid hormone-secreting tumors or assay interference

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of elevated thyroid hormones with non-suppressed TSH and clinical evidence of pituitary resistance after exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing can support diagnosis but is not mandatory; diagnosis primarily based on biochemical and clinical findings.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Inappropriate TSH secretion despite elevated thyroid hormone levels
searchTerms: TSH levels not suppressed despite high thyroid hormones
thyroid hormone excess with normal or high TSH

pathognomonic.symptomName: Elevated serum free thyroxine (FT4) with non-suppressed TSH
searchTerms: high free T4 with non-lowered TSH
thyroid hormone excess without TSH suppression
elevated thyroid hormone and normal TSH

common.symptomName: Palpitations due to thyroid hormone excess
searchTerms: heart palpitations from too much thyroid hormone
rapid heartbeat due to thyroid excess

occasional.symptomName: Weight loss despite normal or increased appetite
searchTerms: unexplained weight loss with normal hunger

rare.symptomName: Visual field defects due to pituitary enlargement
searchTerms: visual field defects due to gland swelling
blind spots caused by pituitary growth

rare.symptomName: Headache related to pituitary mass effect
searchTerms: head pain due to pituitary swelling

rare.symptomName: Delayed bone age or growth abnormalities in children
searchTerms: slow bone growth or delayed skeletal maturity

laboratory: Elevated serum free T4 and free T3 with non-suppressed or elevated TSH
Normal or mildly elevated thyroglobulin levels
Exclusion of thyroid hormone autoantibodies and assay interference
imaging: Pituitary MRI may show normal or mildly enlarged pituitary gland
No evidence of thyroid nodules or autonomous thyroid hormone secretion
genetic: Mutations in thyroid hormone receptor beta (THRB) gene affecting pituitary sensitivity
other: Normal peripheral tissue response to thyroid hormone
Lack of clinical thyrotoxicosis despite elevated thyroid hormone levels

distinguishingFeatures: Resistance to thyroid hormone affecting multiple tissues, not just pituitary
Variable clinical presentation with signs of hypothyroidism and hyperthyroidism
Usually caused by THRB mutations with generalized tissue resistance
Acute severe thyrotoxicosis with systemic decompensation
Clinical emergency with fever, tachycardia, and altered mental status
Pituitary adenoma secreting TSH causing elevated thyroid hormones
Symptoms of hyperthyroidism with elevated or inappropriately normal TSH

redFlags: Persistent elevated TSH despite high thyroid hormone levels
Visual disturbances suggesting pituitary mass effect
Severe cardiovascular symptoms disproportionate to thyroid hormone levels
